'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**[[Israel]] continues [[airstrike]]s in the [[Gaza Strip]], killing several more people, including 42 in [[Gaza City]], which is the deadliest single attack in the past week. The total death toll there rises to 192 people, including 58 children and 34 women. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/16/more-deaths-gaza-israel-launches-most-intense-raids-yet (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Hamas]] fires over 190 rockets at towns and cities in southern [[Israel]], damaging numerous buildings, including a [[synagogue]]. Approximately 3,000 rockets have been fired in the past week. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/southern-communities-pounded-by-gaza-rockets-pm-fighting-will-take-more-time/ (Times of Israel)]
**The [[Israeli Air Force]] destroys the office and home of [[Yahya Sinwar]], the most senior Hamas official in Gaza. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/5/16/israel-destroys-home-of-most-senior-hamas-leader-in-gaza (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Afghan peace process]]
**After discussions in [[Qatar]] and [[Pakistan]], [[Taliban]] representatives have reportedly agreed to substantive talks with the [[Islamic Republic of Afghanistan|Afghan Republic]] team in [[Doha]], and to attend a summit in [[Istanbul]] that they initially refused to attend. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-172195 (TOLO News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Miss Universe 2020]]
**In [[Hollywood, Florida]], [[United States]], [[Andrea Meza]] of [[Mexicana Universal|Mexico]] is crowned [[Miss Universe]]. [https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/lifestyle/artandculture/787751/miss-mexico-is-the-new-miss-universe/story/ (GMA News Online)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Two people are killed and at least 100 others are injured when a tiered seating structure collapses at a partly-built synagogue in [[Giv'at Ze'ev]], in the [[West Bank]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-57138151 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia]]
****The [[Ministry of Health (Indonesia)|Ministry of Health]] suspends the distribution of around 450,000 doses of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] from batch CTMAV547 for toxicity and sterility tests following the death of a 22-year-old man who received the [[vaccine]] 11 days ago. [https://jakartaglobe.id/news/indonesia-suspends-450000-astrazeneca-vaccine-doses-over-postvaccination-death (Jakarta Globe)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education]]
****The [[Singapore]]an [[Ministry of Education (Singapore)|Ministry of Education]] announces that they will close all schools and shift all primary, secondary, and junior college students to full home-based learning beginning May 19 due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases in the community. [https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/parenting-education/spore-schools-to-start-full-home-based-learning-from-may-19-amid-spike (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
****[[Taiwan]] reports a record 207 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, 206 of which are locally transmitted cases. This subsequently brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,682. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/may/16/lockdowns-and-panic-buying-in-taiwan-as-covid-cases-rise (''The Guardian'')] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] surpasses 100,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.thaipbsworld.com/total-covid-19-infections-in-thailand-passed-the-100000-mark-today/ (Thai PBS World)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maine]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****[[Maine]] reports its first case of the Lineage B.1.617 variant that originated in [[India]]. [https://bangordailynews.com/2021/05/16/news/york/coronavirus-variant-first-found-in-india-discovered-in-maine/ (''Bangor Daily News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***[[Algeria]] announces that it will reopen air and land [[border]]s on June 1, but only five flights a day from and to Algerian airports will be allowed as precautions to prevent the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/algeria-reopen-air-land-borders-june-1-2021-05-16/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom]]
***The number of people who have been fully [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccinated]] against COVID-19 in the [[United Kingdom]] surpasses 20 million. [https://news.sky.com/story/covid-19-more-than-20-million-now-fully-vaccinated-in-uk-after-having-both-coronavirus-jabs-12308155 (Sky News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Holy See–Myanmar relations]]
**[[Pope Francis]] condemns the violence and repression in [[Myanmar]] and again condemns the [[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup]] that ousted [[Aung San Suu Kyi]] on February 1. He tells protesters to not despair "in the face of evil or allow themselves to be divided". [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/do-not-give-into-evil-division-pope-tells-myanmar-community-2021-05-16/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[International protests over the 2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**A convoy covered with [[Flag of Palestine|Palestinian flags]] drives through [[North London]] shouting [[Antisemitism|antisemitic]] language. Four people are arrested on suspicion of racially aggravated public order offenses. [https://www.thejc.com/news/uk/pro-palestinian-convoy-tours-north-london-with-speaker-shouting-f-k-the-jews-rape-their-daughters-1.516778 (''The Jewish Chronicle'')] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/london-cops-arrest-4-over-f-the-jews-rape-their-daughters-video/ (''Times of Israel'')]
**In [[Berlin]], violent confrontations break out during a protest against [[Israel]]i airstrikes in the [[Gaza Strip]], with an [[Television in Israel|Israeli TV]] reporter being attacked. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/05/16/clashes-with-police-and-israeli-tv-reporter-attacked-at-pro-palestinian-rally-in-berlin (Euronews)]
**[[Service de police de la Ville de Montréal|Montreal Police]] deploy tear gas to disperse a protest in [[downtown Montreal|downtown]] [[Montreal]], which saw pro-[[Israel]]i protesters clash with pro-[[Palestinians|Palestinian]] protesters. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/pro-israel-protest-montreal-palestine-1.6028966 (CBC)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Chilean Constitutional Convention election]]
**Chileans are summoned to a second consecutive day of voting to elect the 155 members of the [[Constitutional Convention (Chile)|Constitutional Convention]] to change its Pinochet-era constitution. The results show a majority victory for the center-left, with a very important role for independent candidates. [https://elpais.com/internacional/2021-05-16/chile-comienza-a-contar-los-votos-con-la-gran-incognita-de-los-datos-de-participacion.html (''El País'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020–21 UEFA Women's Champions League]]
**[[FC Barcelona Femení|Barcelona]] wins the team's first Champions League after beating [[Chelsea F.C. Women|Chelsea]] in the [[2021 UEFA Women's Champions League Final|final match]] at [[Gamla Ullevi]] in [[Gothenburg]], [[Sweden]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57102472 (BBC Sport)]
